apps.localizedDescription: A free and open-source PlayStation 2 (PS2) emulator based on PCSX2, with native ARM64 JIT recompilers. Play PS2 games on your phone, PC, or gaming handheld.

versions.localizedDescription:
Automated nightly build for community testing (unsigned).

Every download is named `ARMSX2-nightly-DATE-COMMIT-PLATFORM`, so builds
from different nights stay distinguishable after you have downloaded them.

- macOS arm64: macOS-arm64.tar.xz
- Linux arm64: Linux-arm64-4K-pages.AppImage on most distros, or the 16K one on Asahi Linux and other Apple Silicon kernels (run getconf PAGESIZE if unsure)
- Windows arm64: Windows-arm64.zip
- RetroArch on Linux arm64: Linux-arm64-libretro-core.tar.zst, a 4K-page build
- Bare-display kmsdrm handhelds: Linux-arm64-SDL-handheld.tar.zst, a 4K-page build (Rocknix and Batocera run compositors, so use the Qt AppImage there instead)
- Android: Android-arm64.apk (installs as ARMSX2 Nightly, alongside the stable app)
- iOS: iOS-arm64.ipa, unsigned, sideload it (installs as ARMSX2 Nightly, alongside the stable app)

Coming from an old nightly? Nightlies are now a separate app, ARMSX2 Nightly, next to stable.

- Android: stable cannot install over an old nightly. Back up your saves and memory cards, uninstall the old nightly, then install the stable APK.
- iOS: your old nightly is the ARMSX2 iOS app and still has your saves. Copy them into ARMSX2 Nightly with the Files app.

## What's new
- IOP thread: the default lag bound is 24576 EE cycles, up from 6144
- Android: Reset gives back the player's value for a kept key the settings file no longer has
- Android: a resolution auto-tune kept survives the next save from the app
- AutoTune: test that a trial that is not kept never reaches the game's file or the host
- AutoTune: a setting is kept only when the speed rose, never on a lower cost alone
- Android: Reset gives back the value the player set in the app, not the global one
- AutoTune: the EE governor's message says the emulated CPU is underclocked
- AutoTune: say "nothing left to try" once per session, whatever the class
- AutoTune: keep the game database hints and the unsafe settings warning quiet while it applies
- AutoTune: settle 1.5 s, not 3 s, after a light change
- AutoTune: ask the live GS device whether it is Vulkan, not the configuration
- AutoTune: do not offer the GS back thread where it would share a busy core
- AutoTune: try the download mode before the GS back thread for a GPU case
- AutoTune: blending Basic -> Minimum is only tried against the GS on the CPU
- AutoTune: put the cheap levers before the resolution only where they can matter
- AutoTune: the percentage on a kept lever is the measured speed change
- AutoTune: a loss the game's own change explains is not a remembered rejection
- AutoTune: a trial that clearly made things worse is a remembered rejection
- AutoTune: keep on the targeted cost only when the speed did not fall
- AutoTune: tell the Android app about a committed value through a function pointer, not a weak symbol
- AutoTune: judge a trial on medians, on the cost it targets, and against a baseline taken right before it
- AutoTune: tell an IOP-bound case from an EE-bound one by the EE's wait, not the IOP thread's CPU share
- Qt: a game's properties window re-reads its settings file when it comes to the front
- iOS: Automatic Performance Tuning switch in the emulator settings
- Android: setup page asking about Automatic Performance Tuning
- Android: Automatic Performance Tuning switch, and a per-game list and reset
- Android: keep the values auto-tune saves, and let the app read and reset its record
- Host: make the default Host::OnAutoTuneCommitted weak
- AutoTune: the EE governor as a lever
- AutoTune: an EE blocked on the IOP thread is an IOP case, not an EE case
- AutoTune: read the EE's waits and dropped frames from the limiter and wait-site tallies
- EE cycle rate sampler: a tally other consumers can ask for, and one lateness verdict
- Big Picture: setup step asking about Automatic Performance Tuning
- Big Picture: per-game 'Reset Auto-Tune' and the list of what auto-tune changed
- Big Picture: Automatic Performance Tuning switch in the Emulation settings
- Qt: setup wizard page asking about Automatic Performance Tuning
- Qt: per-game 'Reset Auto-Tune' button and the list of what auto-tune changed
- Qt: Automatic Performance Tuning switch on the Emulation settings page
- AutoTune: format the bottleneck report, and say what Resumed does
- AutoTune: a busy GPU outranks busy GS threads; tests for the reset on the game's file
- AutoTune: the applier, and the hooks that run it from the VM
- AutoTune: the sampler that turns a metrics window into a controller window
- EE cycle rate: name the new files in the Windows project
- AutoTune: the per-game settings record, and the reset
- EE cycle rate: a read API for the governor's state and its latest window
- EE cycle rate: do not read CTR_EL0 on Darwin
- EE cycle rate: pin what a per-game opt-in has to write
- EE cycle rate: a charge on a block entry is patchable, not doomed
- EE cycle rate: make the runner say which path a transition took
- EE cycle rate: transition by rewriting the charges, not by resetting
- EE cycle rate: cache maintenance for many patches, one barrier
- EE cycle rate: record where every charge immediate actually sits
- EE cycle rate: classify each charge site's encoding form at emit time
- EE cycle rate: count what a transition actually throws away
- EE cycle rate: time the two halves of a transition separately
- EE cycle rate: keep the session's transition counts out of the controller's reach
- EE cycle rate: only reset on a limiter change that changed the limiter
- EE cycle rate: charge a window's time to the rate it actually ran at
- EE cycle rate: keep the per-frame path a leaf, and stop the trace contradicting itself
- EE cycle rate: in shadow mode the controller has to be told the switch is on
- EE cycle rate: a trace with no windows in it still has to say what it is
- eerunner: --ee-rate-trace, so a scripted run exercises the trace writer
- EE cycle rate: one word for the overlay, and it is the only thing it may read
- EE cycle rate: a trace of every window, and a shadow mode to record it in
- EE cycle rate: close a window at the frame boundary and act on it
- EE cycle rate: time the EE thread's waits on the GS and VU1 threads
- EE cycle rate: what a window's frames add up to, as a pure function
- Perf metrics: one frame-work clock for everyone, not an Android-only one
- EE cycle rate: pin the precedence rules, especially the one about equal values
- EE cycle rate: decide whether the governor may run, and say why
- EE cycle rate: record where the configured selector came from
- EE cycle rate: a dynamic switch, and a trace path the caches ignore
- eerunner: script EE cycle-rate transitions, and time what they cost
- EE cycle rate: give back the step that failed, not the ones that worked
- EE rec: pin the seven cycle-rate selectors, and which selector emitted code uses
- microVU: the EE cycle rate is a VU0-only code-generation input
- EE cycle rate: turn window samples into one step, with no clock and no VM
- EE cycle rate: separate the configured selector from the one we run at
- AutoTune: the decision controller, tested by replaying scripted windows
- PerformanceMetrics: a consistent copy of the last window, and a GPU-timer flag
- Settings: an auto-tune layer above the game layer, and the AutoTune switch
- GS: the 24-bit image writer reads three bytes per pixel, not four
- Controls: all controllers as Player 1, and profiles in the in-game menu
- Setup: an install a launcher has prepared skips the wizard (#847)

Full changelog: https://github.com/ARMSX2/ARMSX2/compare/nightly-20261018...83fe4e293f71ab5587ef81b06143725bf8c6a30b
